title: Temperature Limits for Seed Germination in Industrial Hemp (Cannabis sativa L.)
scope: Cannabis/hemp seed germination percentage and rate across constant temperatures, including cultivar-specific cardinal temperature estimates and priming effects. Use study-specific values as examples, not universal species thresholds.

title: Geographical variation in seed germination of Hemp (Cannabis sativa L.) ecotypes under salinity conditions
publisher: Journal of Applied Research on Medicinal and Aromatic Plants
scope: Cannabis/hemp ecotype variation in germination rate and seedling response as salinity and external water potential decline; supports genotype- and treatment-dependent interpretation.

title: Temperature and Moisture Content for Storage Maintenance of Germination Capacity of Seeds of Industrial Hemp, Marijuana, and Ditchweed Forms of Cannabis sativa
scope: Long-term Cannabis seed germination capacity under combinations of storage temperature and seed moisture; supports storage-condition effects without assigning a universal shelf life.

title: Seed Priming and Pericarp Removal Improve Germination in Low-Germinating Seed Lots of Industrial Hemp
scope: Low-germinating hemp seed lots, pericarp removal, osmotic or solid-matrix priming, vigor, and seedling recovery; supports context-dependent treatment effects rather than guaranteed rescue.

title: Diversity of root system architecture and root-shoot biomass allocation in industrial hemp (Cannabis sativa L.)
scope: Cannabis/hemp variation in total root length, root-system shape, lateral-root fraction, biomass allocation, heritability, and candidate root-architecture genes across diverse genotypes.

title: Root-TRAPR: a modular plant growth device to visualize root development and monitor growth parameters, as applied to an elicitor response of Cannabis sativa
scope: Time-resolved Cannabis root growth and morphology, including increasing length, surface area, and formation of new lateral roots in a controlled imaging system.

title: Morphoanatomical, histochemical, and molecular characterization of female Cannabis plants from three Argentine strains
scope: Cannabis root anatomy including primary versus adventitious-root tissue organization and early secondary development; useful for Cannabis-specific tissue context.

title: Aquaporins in Plants
scope: General vascular-plant aquaporin biology and regulated membrane water permeability. Used only for mechanisms that lack Cannabis-specific measurements; not evidence for Cannabis-specific flux rates.

title: Back to the roots: Cannabis sativa L. root metabolism, microbiomes, and biotechnological potential
scope: Cannabis root metabolism, exudation, rhizosphere/endosphere microbiomes, and plant-microbe interactions; supports context-dependent association rather than guaranteed benefit.

title: An X-linked sex determination mechanism in cannabis and hop
scope: Phased Cannabis sex chromosomes, X/Y evolution, and an X-linked ACS/ethylene-pathway mechanism associated with female inflorescence fate; supports chromosome-level context while avoiding one-gene explanations for all sex expression.

title: Sex-specific ethylene responses drive floral sexual plasticity in Cannabis sativa
scope: Multi-omic Cannabis evidence for sex-specific ethylene responses during induced floral sex change in XX and XY plants; distinguishes chromosome complement from phenotypic floral plasticity.

title: Hermaphroditism in Marijuana (Cannabis sativa L.) Inflorescences – Impact on Floral Morphology, Seed Formation, Progeny Sex Ratios, and Genetic Variation
scope: Cannabis anther morphology, longitudinal dehiscence, pollen release and germination observations, and mixed-sex reproductive structures.

title: Development and Optimization of a Germination Assay and Long-Term Storage for Cannabis sativa Pollen
scope: Cannabis pollen germination assays, collection-stage effects, loss of viability during cool storage, desiccation/cryopreservation methods, and periodic viability testing.

title: Methods for characterizing pollen fitness in Cannabis sativa L.
scope: Cannabis pollen non-abortion versus in-vitro germination, demonstrating that staining-based integrity and actual germination are distinct measures and that viability declines with time after dehiscence.

title: Photosynthetic response of Cannabis sativa L. to variations in photosynthetic photon flux densities, temperature and CO2 conditions
publisher: Physiology and Molecular Biology of Plants
scope: Cannabis leaf gas exchange under varying PPFD, temperature, and CO2; supports coupled response teaching while keeping experimental genotype and chamber conditions explicit.

title: Supplemental greenhouse lighting increased the water use efficiency, crop growth, and cutting production in Cannabis sativa
scope: Cannabis responses to contrasting daily light integrals and short-term PPFD, including photosynthetic acclimation and water-use responses; supports separating DLI from instantaneous PPFD.

title: Characterization of Nutrient Disorders of Cannabis sativa
scope: Controlled single-nutrient deficiency and toxicity symptom progression paired with Cannabis tissue analysis; supports visual-plus-analytical diagnosis rather than image-only conclusions.

title: Foliar Symptomology, Nutrient Content, Yield, and Secondary Metabolite Variability of Cannabis Grown Hydroponically with Different Single-Element Nutrient Deficiencies
scope: Cannabis nutrient-deficiency symptom onset and progression with upper/lower canopy tissue analysis; shows that visual onset and foliar elemental analysis do not always align simply.

title: Integrated Management of Pathogens and Microbes in Cannabis sativa L. (Cannabis) under Greenhouse Conditions
scope: Cannabis root/crown, foliar, floral, and systemic disease patterns plus integrated diagnostics; explicitly notes that root browning can arise from pathogens or waterlogging and that confirmation matters.

title: Challenges to Cannabis sativa Production from Pathogens and Microbes—The Role of Molecular Diagnostics and Bioinformatics
scope: Cannabis pathogen identification with PCR-based and genomic diagnostics, supporting confirmatory testing when visual disease symptoms are non-specific.
